raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not chase fancy things. On my 9 mu, wheat and maize have fed the family for many years, and this double crop is still the safest for me. I have only 2 people at home, so I follow the local timing and use what is easy to manage. If wheat misses the autumn moisture or maize goes in late after wheat harvest, the whole year suffers. So I will keep the same wheat-maize rotation on all 9 mu.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, around the village usual time. I will use a common improved wheat seed from the local dealer, not the expensive special kind. I usually put most fertilizer at sowing, then look at the crop after winter. If the leaves are pale and the stand is not strong at jointing, I topdress again. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times, only at the key stages. Wheat is the crop I do not dare short too much, because if it gets weak over winter or at jointing, yield drops badly.

For maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest, fast, with little delay. That gap is very short in Quzhou, so I will use rotary tillage or direct seeding after the combine if I can get the machine in time. I will buy hybrid maize seed like most neighbors do. Maize grows fast if there is summer rain, so I do not plan heavy irrigation unless the weather turns dry. I will still put fertilizer, but not too much all at once. At my age and with small land, I want a steady harvest, not to spend too much cash at the start and then worry later.
